case.pattern_description: A single device profile (Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080) was used on 138 different cards between 2016-11-01 and 2016-12-31. It was recorded as new to every account it touched and sat behind an anonymising proxy on every transaction, which is not how a genuinely shared device behaves -- a household or office device shows returning users. The purchases are small and spread thinly across many cards, so no single cardholder looks alarming; the pattern is only visible as a shared-device cluster across the portfolio.

evidence.claim: Transaction used a device profile shared with 138 cards, known in fraud ring.
Four transactions occurred within 30 minutes on same device profile, indicating repeat use.
Transaction amounts (~$480) are far above the card's baseline median $62.93 and 90th percentile $226.08.
Prior closed cases with same shared device pattern were confirmed fraud, with exposures > $1,000.

case.summary: The cardholder denied the high‑value online purchase and the activity matches an undocumented shared‑device fraud ring that has produced multiple confirmed fraud cases. The burst of four large transactions far exceeds the card’s normal spending pattern. Combined with the denial and ring membership, the evidence strongly points to fraud, warranting a card block and case creation.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: The cardholder maintains they did not make the transaction and still holds the card.

sar.narrative: The subject of this report is customer C07297, who holds payment card C07297‑K1. Four online transactions using product code C were processed on that card, totaling $1,906.07. The transactions occurred between 2016‑11‑21 20:00:00 and 2016‑11‑21 20:30:00. All activity was conducted via the online channel from a desktop browser identified as Trident/7.0 on Windows 7, Internet Explorer 11.0, with a screen resolution of 1920 × 1080. The pattern of activity is undocumented, and the device profile used for these four transactions is shared with 138 other cards, appearing as a new profile for each linked account and anonymised on every transaction. The same device profile is also associated with a series of other cards, including C00288‑K1, C00329‑K2, C00452‑K2, C00502‑K1, C00555‑K1, C00626‑K1, C00679‑K1, C00750‑K2, C00854‑K2, C00892‑K1, C00941‑K1, and C01104‑K2. The cardholder has asserted that they did not make the transactions and that they continue to possess the physical card. The combination of an undocumented transaction pattern, a device profile that is simultaneously new to each linked account yet shared across 138 cards, and similarity to prior cases CC‑5254, CC‑5111, CC‑4199, CC‑4124, and CC‑4086 raises a strong suspicion of fraudulent activity. Accordingly, the activity meets the criteria for a suspicious transaction report.

stop_reason: The cardholder's response (denied) settles the question; further steps would not change the recommended actions.
